title: Polestar Systems - Implementation Onboarding Kickoff

Agreed next steps: share runbook, security matrix, schedule pilot benchmark window, and coordinate networking contacts.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-16
Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jasper (Redwood AE), Eliot (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Anika, Marcus, Sofia, Tom (Polestar)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on Dedicated deployment and pilot scope.

[00:00] Jasper: Hey everyone, welcome — thanks for making time. I'm Jasper from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intro from folks?
[00:28] Anika: Hi I'm Anika Rao, head of platform at Polestar. We're running a mix of internal services and some third-party infra, looking to offload ML inference to something more predictable.
[00:45] Marcus: Marcus Liu, IT ops. I'll own the network bits and infra connectivity.
[01:05] Sofia: Sofia Alvarez, security. We'll need to review logs, KMS integration, and compliance artifacts.
[01:20] Tom: Tom Greer, eng manager, I'll coordinate engineering side and pilot success criteria.
[01:36] Jasper: Awesome. Eliot and Maya are on deck — Eliot is our solutions engineer who'll run through the technical approach, Maya will be your CSM for onboarding. Eliot, want to give a quick runtime overview?
[01:55] Eliot: Sure, thanks. So Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools. For pilot we typically recommend a small pool to validate latency and throughput with your actual traffic shapes. We can tune batching and KV cache to meet token cost and latency targets.
[02:22] Tom: When you say KV cache, sorry could you explain that quickly — is that session cache?
[02:33] Eliot: Yeah, KV cache is the transformer key/value cache; it saves context between requests — helps for chat-like flows. For many customers it's a big win because you avoid re-computing earlier tokens.
[02:52] Jasper: For Polestar, based on your notes, I think two pilot goals: one, verify 95th percentile latency under 250ms for core endpoints; two, measure per-token cost for your longest prompt path. Does that sound right?
[03:12] Tom: That aligns but we'll need to confirm exact endpoints. We'll share traffic patterns.
[03:30] Anika: A few constraints — we have strict data residency needs for logs, plus we use a centralized KMS for keys. We can't have persistent copies of raw data leave our VPC.
[03:48] Maya: Understood. We have private deployment options, and for Dedicated we support VPC peering and private networking. We'll also provide an encrypted audit log stream that you can ingest.
[04:10] Sofia: On audit logs — what retention and fields are included? We need user-level tokens redaction and proof of deletion if required.
[04:28] Eliot: Our standard audit includes request IDs, model used, token counts, timestamps, and error traces. We redacted PII in logs by default and can provide log filters. For deletion, we can demonstrate lifecycle policies and provide exportable ledger for audits. I'll pull the security docs after this call.
[04:56] Anika: Cool. Also wondering about private key management — can you integrate with our AWS KMS or HashiCorp?
[05:12] Jasper: Yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS, GCP) and can discuss HSM options for Private deployments. For Dedicated we typically integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest keys.
[05:34] Marcus: For networking: we'll need IP ranges, expected egress, and firewall rules. Also we have strict change windows so scheduling matters.
[05:48] Maya: We'll provide a network requirements doc and a sample infra diagram. We'll also coordinate with your change windows for any peering operations.
[06:10] Tom: Pilot timeline — how long do you expect the pilot to run? 2 weeks? 4 weeks?
[06:24] Eliot: Usually a 2–4 week pilot. Two weeks is enough to validate latency and basic stability; four weeks gives you more sample size for cost metrics. We recommend 3 weeks as a pragmatic middle ground.
[06:45] Jasper: For deliverables: onboarding runbook, bench script, access checklist, and initial SLO targets. We'll also set weekly checkpoints.
[07:02] Anika: On access — we prefer just-in-time VM bastion access and limited service accounts. We don't want permanent external keys.
[07:20] Eliot: We support temporary credentials and role-based access. For the pilot we can issue scoped tokens for the Redwood console and API.
[07:38] Sofia: About compliance artifacts — can you share your SOC2 report, ISO scope, and pen test summary?
[07:52] Jasper: Yes. I'll attach our compliance pack. Some of it is NDA-protected so we'll send via secure share.
[08:05] Anika: One thing — we plan to run heavy batch generation for a portion of the pilot. How do you handle autoscaling and burst?
[08:20] Eliot: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and short-term burst capacity. For cost predictability we can pin baseline capacity and allow controlled bursts; we'll instrument usage to prevent runaway costs.
[08:39] Tom: Are there tooling hooks for tracing user requests end-to-end with our app?
[08:50] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns. We can add tracing hooks to correlate request IDs across systems.
[09:05] Marcus: We'll need a logging endpoint — can you push logs to our Splunk/ELK?
[09:16] Eliot: Push to Splunk via HEC, or forward to S3/Cloud Storage for ingestion. We'll include sample config in the network doc.
[09:30] Jasper: Let's talk success metrics — Tom, you mentioned 95th p95 latency under 250ms and cost per 1k tokens under a threshold. Anything else?
[09:46] Tom: Also error rate below 0.5% for production-like load, and qualitative acceptance on hallucination for a set of prompt suites we'll share.
[10:01] Anika: For SVU (sensitive value usage), we can't send PHI to third-party models. We have a classification layer that filters or masks data before inference. We'll test that as part of pilot.
[10:20] Eliot: Good — we can run the masked data and a small unmasked set in a controlled environment to validate.
[10:35] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[10:45] Jasper: Ok next, roles and calendar — Maya will run the weekly standups. We'll set initial onboarding tasks and assign owners.
[10:58] Maya: I'll schedule 30-minute weekly check-ins. First one will be next Monday 2026-01-26. I'll also create a Slack channel for day-to-day.
[11:12] Anika: We'll invite our security and infra leads.
[11:20] Marcus: For IP allowlist, what's the format you need? CIDR or hostnames?
[11:28] Eliot: CIDR ranges are preferred; we'll also accept peering setup details. We'll share our egress and VIP ranges.
[11:42] Jasper: For benchmarking, Eliot will propose a config: model variant a smaller open model and a production-like larger variant to compare latency/cost tradeoffs.
[11:58] Eliot: We'll include quantized variants and recommended batching sizes per endpoint. Also will include tokenization calculator so you can map tokens to invoice units.
[12:18] Tom: Onboarding docs — do you have runbooks for rollback and emergency isolation? We need quick steps in case of incidents.
[12:33] Maya: Yes, our runbook includes isolation playbook, temporary key revocation, and a kill switch for immediate traffic reroute. We'll highlight those in the doc.
[12:50] Sofia: Can we get an SLA for Dedicated? Uptime and latency SLOs?
[13:03] Jasper: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency tiers depending on reserved commit. We'll include the SLA summary; enterprise terms can be negotiated in the contract.
[13:22] Anika: Pricing — can you provide an estimate for the pilot and a projected 12-month run rate?
[13:34] Jasper: I can send a pilot estimate and a model showing committed vs variable costs. For Dedicated there are reserved capacity options that reduce per-token cost.
[13:48] Tom: One technical deep dive question: how do you handle model rollouts and automatic fallback? Say a new model version has regressions.
[14:02] Eliot: We support canary deploys and A/B rollouts with automatic rollback based on error rates and quality signals. For regressions tied to prompt sets we have eval hooks to detect quality drops.
[14:24] Marcus: For network latency, what about region placement — can we keep traffic inside us-east-1 only?
[14:35] Jasper: Yes, we can pin deployments to region and support routing policies to prefer a region or fallback to another if needed.
[14:48] Anika: About data residency — logs and analytics must remain in-region. Is that configurable?
[14:58] Eliot: Yes, retention location is configurable per-customer. We'll outline the options in the compliance doc.
[15:12] Jasper: Ok I'm going to list immediate deliverables: onboarding runbook, network requirements sheet, security/compliance pack, and bench script. Anything else?
[15:27] Sofia: Please include proof points for pen tests and SOC2 coverage dates. We also want data encryption details at rest and in transit.
[15:38] Jasper: Noted. We'll send cert dates and encryption details.
[15:45] Anika: For the pilot dataset — we will provide a sanitized dataset and a small live traffic mirror.
[15:55] Eliot: Great — if you can send a sample size metric (rps, average tokens, peak tokens) that will help us size the pool.
[16:10] Tom: We'll share typical and worst-case traffic patterns by tomorrow.
[16:22] Jasper: On timelines — propose we kick pilot week of 2026-01-26, with benching the first 3 days and then a 2-week observable window. Is that acceptable?
[16:36] Anika: Yes that fits our quarterly roadmap.
[16:45] Marcus: One operational question — do you support role-based access controls for team members so we can limit who can change model variants?
[16:57] Maya: Yes, RBAC is supported; we can create viewer, operator, admin roles. We'll map to your SAML groups if needed.
[17:12] Tom: Regarding cost controls — is there a hard cap or alerting you can configure?
[17:25] Eliot: Alerts and soft caps exist; hard caps are possible but might require fallback behavior to a cheaper model. We'll document options.
[17:40] Anika: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[17:47] Jasper: None from our side — just need the networking contacts and the compliance questionnaire responses. Once we have those we'll prepare the trial environment.
[18:00] Sofia: For compliance questionnaire, we'll fill it and route to you via secure share.
[18:12] Jasper: Great. Quick recap and owners: Jasper runbook & pricing, Eliot bench script, Maya scheduling, Anika/Polestar provide network and compliance artifacts.
[18:30] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[18:38] Jasper: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and invites.
[47:58] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has minor transcription errors typical of call exports; some overlapping talk noted. Shared artifacts to be attached: onboarding-runbook-v1.pdf (link: [secure share pending]), network-requirements-template.xlsx, redwood-compliance-pack.zip.
